Schema 3 architecture

Source: vignettes/articles/contributor-schema-architecture.Rmd
contributor-schema-architecture.Rmd

Contributing · Object model · Discovery walkthrough · Object fields

This documents the implemented R object model, not a proposed hierarchy. The public sceptre_object coordinates five persisted components and records schema_version = 3L. Numerical fitting, sampling, scoring, integration and adjustment remain ordinary functions. CellView is a small transient S4 value. There is no saved Nextflow execution mode or pipeline compatibility claim.

The exact current slot/type inventory is OBJECT_FIELDS.md. FIELD_DECISIONS.md accounts for every field in the physical schema 1 and schema 2 fixtures, including removed fields and migration limits.

Authority and representations

Owner Authoritative payload Important boundary
sceptre_object data, spec, preparation, fits, results, schema version No duplicate workflow flags or call journal.
ScreenData Normalized response/guide counts, source cell covariates, canonical guide metadata, display response names, MOI, imported assignment summaries, content identity Count-store row names are canonical response IDs; response_names is display annotation. Modalities share aligned cells, not features.
AnalysisSpec Resolved scientific choices, canonical requested discovery/positive-control pairs, assignment and QC settings No second requested snapshot, budgets, sampled calibration family or worker settings.
PreparationRecord Compiled design/pairs/groups, durable guide assignments, selected cells and QC payloads, stage identities Distinct source and analysis coordinates; assignments exist before QC.
FitCache Compact response and CRT perturbation model fits with independent identities No cell-length fitted vectors or sampled draws.
ResultRecord Completed entries owning their table, provenance, scope, identity and history; legacy import metadata A saved table can remain readable while historical.
CellView Ordered source/analysis/fit mappings and treatment positions Built on demand, without copied full count matrices or an eager view per group.

Canonical requested pair tables in spec retain target/response request order and multiplicity. preparation@discovery_pairs and @positive_control_pairs are compiled guide-group expansions. Their *_with_info tables additionally retain nonzero counts and pass_qc, including requests that fail QC. Canonical guide metadata exists once in data; preparation stores only its row-aligned guide_groups vector. guide_group_metadata() constructs the joined view.

Counts are stored directly as CountStore = dgRMatrix | BackedCountStore | NULL; NULL accommodates initialization and recognizable missing legacy stores, not a usable imported screen. BackedCountStore has a typed CountHandle = externalptr | NULL and one descriptor:

BackedCountStore
  descriptor: list(
    path: character[1], content_md5: character[1],
    dimensions: integer[2], dimnames: list(response/guide IDs, cell labels or NULL),
    integer_id: integer[1])
  handle: process-local external pointer or NULL

Descriptor dimensions/labels remain available while closed. Numerical access unwraps a live store and requires reopening. ondisc is optional (Suggests); in-memory work neither installs nor loads it. Reopening validates anchored file content, dimensions, labels and import ID. Verified relocation changes path and handle without changing scientific identity. The import ID alone proves no content equivalence. Saving verifies the anchored descriptor and removes live handles; it does not replace the old content anchor with a new file checksum. Backing files are immutable during analysis: getters and per-gene loops do not scan for unsupported external file edits.

Nested preparation and choice payloads

All indices below are one-based R positions. Ordered identities preserve order; membership helpers explicitly perform any deduplication or ordering required by the existing procedure.

ScreenData.import_grna_assignment_info
  max_grna: source-cell-aligned guide labels
  max_grna_frac_umis: source-cell-aligned numeric fractions

AnalysisSpec.grna_assignment_hyperparameters
  maximum: umi_fraction_threshold, min_grna_n_umis_threshold
  thresholding: threshold
  mixture: n_em_rep, pi_guess_range, g_pert_guess_range,
           n_nonzero_cells_cutoff, backup_threshold,
           probability_threshold, formula_object
AnalysisSpec.cellwise_qc_thresholds
  response_n_umis_range, response_n_nonzero_range, p_mito_threshold
AnalysisSpec.additional_cells_to_remove: integer source-cell positions

PreparationRecord.guide_assignments
  <guide ID>: integer source-cell positions
PreparationRecord.source_groups
  grna_group_idxs: named lists of source-cell memberships
  indiv_nt_grna_idxs: named lists of source-cell memberships
PreparationRecord.analysis_groups
  grna_group_idxs: named lists of positions in analysis_cells
  indiv_nt_grna_idxs: named NT memberships
  all_nt_idxs: ordered positions in analysis_cells (NT-control mode only)
PreparationRecord.stages
  design | assignment | cell_qc | pair_qc: list(identity = SHA-256 value)

With complement controls, analysis_groups$indiv_nt_grna_idxs indexes analysis_cells. With NT controls it indexes all_nt_idxs, which itself indexes analysis_cells. CellView resolves this distinction into source_cells, fit_to_analysis, trt_fit_pos, and n_trt; counts and design rows use exactly that order. Complement response fits use all QC cells. NT calibration uses the ordered NT list; NT discovery/power fits treatment plus NT cells per group and does not relabel those fits as a global reusable response cache.

Preparation lifecycle and fitting

The prerequisite chain is import → design → assignment → cell QC → pair QC. Each preparation stage is committed only after successful computation and validation. The existence of a matching stage identity, together with valid prerequisites, establishes completion; there is no saved complete Boolean. workflow_status(object) derives public workflow status from these stage identities and current result records.

Beginning design removes all preparation stage records; beginning assignment removes assignment/cell-QC/pair-QC records; beginning cell QC removes both QC records; beginning pair QC removes its record. These transitions mark existing result entries with invalidated_by, retaining their tables and history. Formula environments are excluded from stable identity values; compiled design values, dimensions, contrasts/attributes and ordering still participate in the relevant fingerprints. Failed calls return no partially committed object.

The response family has one explicit fitting scope:

FitCache.response_fits
  <canonical response ID>: list(fitted_coefs = named numeric vector,
                                theta = positive numeric scalar)
FitCache.response_identity
  data: imported content identity
  cells: ordered integer source cells actually fitted
  columns: ordered design column names
  design: SHA-256 of actual selected design values and attributes
  method: "poisson-glm.fit-then-dispersion-v1"

Cache lookup is admitted only for a matching fitting identity. Parameter setters, low-MOI reassignment and retained-cell changes additionally clear incompatible fits. High-MOI reassignment can retain response fits when their actual fitting inputs remain unchanged, while tests/results are invalidated. Pair eligibility can change without changing the cells or response fits. Content replacement clears preparation and fits and invalidates results.

The algorithm remains Poisson glm.fit followed by dispersion estimation at Poisson means; the method identifier does not claim a negative-binomial refit.

The independent perturbation family stores actual CRT logistic models:

FitCache.perturbation_fits
  <prepared guide group>: list(
    fitted_coefs = named numeric vector,
    diagnostics = list(rank, converged, boundary, iterations, warnings),
    identity = list(cells = SHA-256, design = SHA-256, treatment = SHA-256))
FitCache.perturbation_identity
  cells: ordered analysis source cells (stored once)
  columns, design: common design columns and actual selected values fingerprint
  method: "binomial-glm.fit-linkinv-v1"
  runtime: R, stats, BLAS, matprod

The per-group hashes bind the ordered cells actually fitted, their actual design and binary treatment indicator. In low-MOI NT mode these are treatment plus NT cells in their numerical order; a group label or common context alone cannot certify a hit. Neither entries nor common NT metadata repeat per-group cell vectors. Cache admission requires finite coefficients and bit-exact reproduction of the original fitted probabilities using the original matrix product, zero offset and binomial inverse link. Aliased, nonfinite or inexact fits still execute once and remain uncached. Warnings occur on actual fits and are not replayed on warm hits. Every run draws a fresh full CRT bank; no random draws are cached.

Assignment reruns clear perturbation fits at either MOI. Actual fitting-cell or design changes invalidate the corresponding family; reporting choices can retain both families. Calibration bypasses perturbation cache reads and writes, retaining existing discovery fits. Workers return fit proposals; no family is committed before all workers and result finalization succeed.

PR #233, reviewed at head 3f1ff0650078b382662ee70b72ea5c72fa15b031, supplies the precedent for compact coefficients, exact inverse-link reconstruction, fresh draws, calibration bypass and cold-fit warnings. This model places both families in one typed owner with independent identities, uses shared NT context plus per-entry actual-input hashes, and handles old physical layouts explicitly at migration boundaries. It does not adopt the PR’s flat cache slot or legacy forwarding accessors.

Transient run plans and committed results

A private RunPlan is an S4 value. Calibration preparation returns the ordinary wrapper list(object, plan); its execution phase takes the typed plan explicitly. Public workflow signatures retain their familiar object-in/object-out behavior. RunPlan is temporary during preparation and execution, then frozen in a completed result’s provenance. It is not a second working settings authority.

RunPlan
  analysis: run_calibration_check | run_power_check | run_discovery_analysis
  pairs: complete prepared family, including failed-QC rows
  B1, B2, B3: validated integer budgets
  n_calibration_pairs, calibration_group_size: positive integer scalars for calibration,
    integer(0) outside calibration
  identity:
    data, cells, design, assignments,
    choices: side/approximation/control/resampling/integration/reporting settings
    execution: SHA-256 of the plan payload excluding identity

Structural validity enforces one canonical analysis, prepared identity/QC columns, scalar nonnegative integer budgets with a safe total, and coherent calibration-only size fields. Screen-context validation separately checks canonical response IDs, prepared guide/NT membership and the actual input identity. Empty noncalibration scopes and repeated hypothesis rows remain legitimate numerical requests; they do not bypass complete-family commit guards. The selected pair table is owned independently of mutable caller tables.

run_plan_payload() exposes one ordered plain value for hashing and boundary conversion. It restores explicitly named NULL calibration fields for noncalibration plans, preserving the pre-RunPlan execution-hash contract. No $, $<- or indexing compatibility generic is installed for RunPlan. Known old schema 3 list plans convert only at the boundary, keeping their original identity rather than signing a new one. Result history receives the same conversion. Unknown or malformed payloads remain inspectable as historical migration evidence rather than becoming current plans.

Normal plans derive the existing budget policy: B1 = 499; skew-normal B2 = 4999 and B3 = 24999 for permutations or 0 for CRT. Empirical plans use B2 = 0 and the existing compute_empirical_budget() rule. Calibration uses its requested family size; discovery/power use the maximum of their passing-family counts. pair_count(..., passing = FALSE) counts canonical requested target-response rows. Passing Bonferroni counts target-response families with at least one eligible guide; other strategies use their established passing compiled-row count. A private explicit-budget seam supports numerical fixtures/extensions; public workflows do not expose arbitrary resampling-budget overrides.

Plans bind actual data/design/ordered cells/assignments, canonical feature IDs, eligible guide memberships and execution scope. Payload/input changes invalidate the plan. Calibration choices never mutate working Spec budgets, so a later calibration cannot overwrite a previous discovery run’s realized budget.

Permutation execution shares the full B1+B2+B3 draw bank across the run; CRT shares a full bank within each guide group. Traversal, native RNGs and draw consumption remain in the existing numerical drivers.

ResultRecord.records[<public analysis name>]
  table: finalized data frame
  scope: "complete_family"
  identity: frozen run-plan identity
  provenance:
    schema_version, package_version
    spec: value snapshot of resolved choices (formula language, no environment)
    plan: full realized RunPlan and selected family
    output_amount
    response_fit_method: "poisson-glm.fit-then-dispersion-v1"
  history: list of previous entries, each without another nested history list
  invalidated_by: optional reason
ResultRecord.import_metadata
  migrated_from_schema, provenance, discarded_unverified_fit_count,
  canonical_requests, optional legacy_backend_id

Committing requires current QC, a matching plan, full finalized family key coverage (including legitimate duplicate requests), numeric p-values in [0,1] or missing, and complete-family adjustment for calibration/discovery. Power retains its established grouped-result semantics. Noncalibration subset plans cannot be committed as a complete prepared family. Public analyses always finalize whole families; there is no live raw-shard result mode.

Currentness requires valid QC, a committed table, complete_family scope, matching current inputs/family, and no invalidated_by. Historical validity is separate: get_result(..., historical = TRUE) returns the retained table with its record attached and warns when it is not current. Plotting, getters and export use the same current-result guard. Preparing or failing a rerun leaves the previous committed result intact; successful reruns archive its entry.

Migration inspects physical serialized attributes, not the new registered slot list. It preserves recognized data/QC payloads, result tables and saved result history, reconstructs canonical requests only when the saved traversal is recognizable, and marks old result/fit provenance unknown. It does not certify old flags, fit reuse, old statistical methods or Nextflow compatibility. See the explicit retention/removal inventory in FIELD_DECISIONS.md.
